summary: The SEC's Final Orders page (Wayback capture of 10 Nov 2025) lists 970 final orders on award claims from July 2012 to 30 Sept 2025: 324 award (or award-and-denial) documents and 646 denial or bar documents. All 324 award PDFs were downloaded from the Wayback Machine and read; 93 were already in the dataset by release number and 9 more by date and amount, so 222 new award orders were added (plus 3 already-listed orders whose percentage was missing), as 258 case rows: 208 with a dollar amount, 34 with only a percentage, 16 with both redacted. Amounts are as printed in the orders ('more than', 'approximately'…), usually the award recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission, based on sanctions collected so far, so they are not amounts paid. Covered actions are redacted in every award order except the 2013 Hicks/Locust Offshore orders. The 644 denial and bar orders are recorded one row per listed document (outcome denied) from the list page; the SEC states no yearly denial count there. Two SEC press releases fill gaps (2014 additional payment; April 2020 $27m award date). For the CFTC, press releases and award orders add amounts for 11 orders that had none (four of them only as one combined total) (2014, 2015, 16-WB-06, 16-WB-08, 22-WB-02, 24-WB-09 to -12 as a total, 26-WB-01, 26-WB-07, plus a partial $4,247.22 payment in 24-WB-03 and a 20% share in 24-WB-02); 18 granted CFTC orders still have no amount because the CFTC withholds it. No web searches were used.

cases.target: Locust Offshore Management, LLC; Andrey C. Hicks
cases.summary: Award to three whistleblowers who helped the SEC shut down a sham hedge fund (5% each).
cases.quote: claims each are approved in the amount of 5%
cases.notes: Exchange Act Release No. 69749, File No. 2013-1. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (June 12, 2013). Whistleblowers awarded: 3 (Claimants #1, #2 and #3, 5% each; Claimant #4 denied). The order gives no dollar amount and the percentage is redacted. award_pct is the share for each of the three claimants. The covered action is named in the order: SEC v. Andrey C. Hicks and Locust Offshore Management, LLC (D. Mass. 2011). The order also states the court-ordered disgorgement and civil penalties ($2,512,058.39 each item); amounts collected are not given.

cases.summary: First CFTC whistleblower award; amount as of the order date.
cases.quote: as of the date of this order, will exceed $240,000
cases.notes: Order WB-APP 2014-02-19-01 (decision issued 19 May 2014). "Will exceed": value is the lower bound. Percentage redacted.

cases.summary: CFTC announces its first whistleblower award.
cases.location: para 1
cases.notes: Same award as order WB-APP 2014-02-19-01 (19 May 2014). "Approximately".

cases.summary: Second CFTC award: one applicant awarded, a second applicant denied.
cases.quote: as of the date of this order, will exceed $290,000
cases.notes: Order WB-APP (redacted), date from the whistleblower.gov list (result "Granted; Denied"). "Will exceed": lower bound. 1 whistleblower awarded, 1 denied.

cases.summary: CFTC announces an award to one whistleblower.
cases.location: para 1
cases.quote: it will make an award of approximately $290,000 to a whistleblower
cases.notes: Same award as the redacted WB-APP order of 29 Sept 2015. The FY2015 annual report rounds it to "approximately $300,000" (separate row). "Approximately".

cases.summary: Then-largest CFTC award, to one whistleblower.
cases.location: para 1
cases.quote: announced an award of more than $10 million to a whistleblower
cases.notes: Award Determination 16-WB-06 (order dated 28 March 2016 in the whistleblower.gov list). "More than": lower bound.

cases.summary: Fourth CFTC award, to one whistleblower.
cases.location: para 1
cases.quote: announced an award of approximately $50,000 to a whistleblower
cases.notes: Award Determination 16-WB-08 (order dated 19 July 2016 in the whistleblower.gov list). "Approximately".

cases.summary: Awards to two whistleblowers whose information expanded an existing investigation.
cases.location: para 1
cases.quote: announced awards totaling approximately $500,000 to two whistleblowers
cases.notes: Award Determination 22-WB-02 (order dated 10 March 2022 per the whistleblower.gov list; result "Granted; Denied"). Whistleblowers: 2. Total for both; "approximately".

cases.summary: Four orders on one day granting awards to seven whistleblowers (fraud victims, a market participant, a compliance employee) in CFTC and related actions.
cases.location: para 1
cases.quote: announced awards totaling approximately $4.5 million for whistleblowers
cases.notes: Award Determinations 24-WB-09, 24-WB-10, 24-WB-11, 24-WB-12 (all 23 Sept 2024). Whistleblowers: 7 ("to a total of seven whistleblowers"). Total of the four orders; "approximately". Amounts per order not given.

cases.summary: Awards to two whistleblowers in cases involving defrauded investors.
cases.location: para 1
cases.quote: it is awarding more than $1.8 million to two whistleblowers
cases.notes: Award Determination 26-WB-01 (order dated 17 Dec 2025 per the whistleblower.gov list; result "Granted; Denied"). Whistleblowers: 2. "More than": lower bound.

cases.summary: Awards to five whistleblowers in a fraud case with a substantial recovery for investors.
cases.location: para 1
cases.quote: it is awarding more than $8 million to five whistleblowers
cases.notes: Award Determination 26-WB-07 (1 June 2026). Whistleblowers: 5. "More than": lower bound. The release says the CFTC does not disclose the exact award amount.

cases.summary: Award to one claimant on a CFTC covered action and a related action; a second claimant denied. Payment so far on the covered action is small because little has been collected.
cases.quote: collected, resulting in a payment of payment of $4,247.22
cases.notes: Award Determination 24-WB-03. Amount is the payment on the covered action based on sanctions collected to date (the quote repeats "payment of" as printed); the award percentages and the related-action payment are redacted, so the total award is unknown.

cases.summary: Award to one claimant whose tip opened the case but who gave limited further help; a second claimant denied.
cases.quote: an award of 20% to Claimant 1 is appropriate
cases.notes: Award Determination 24-WB-02. The ordering paragraph redacts the percentage; 20% is stated in the Commission's reasoning. Amount not given.

gaps: SEC orders after 30 Sept 2025 (FY2026) not covered: the latest archived capture of the Final Orders page is 10 Nov 2025 and lists nothing after 30 Sept 2025; sec.gov blocks scripted access to the live page.

SEC denials by fiscal year: the Final Orders page gives no counts, so nothing is counted here (as instructed). Each listed denial document is a case row; 171 documents are labelled 'Denial Orders' (plural) and may cover several claimants or claims, which the list does not say. The denial PDFs themselves were not downloaded or read.

SEC award orders without a dollar amount: 34 rows give only a percentage (mostly 30%) and 16 rows have both amount and percentage redacted. The SEC press releases for those dates give headline totals that mix several orders, so they were not split per order.
Number of whistleblowers per SEC order is read from the ordering paragraph; for joint awards to claimants collectively called 'Claimant 1' the number is not stated (noted in the row).

Covered action names: redacted in all SEC award orders read, except SEC v. Andrey C. Hicks and Locust Offshore Management (D. Mass. 2011) and the related criminal case United States v. Hicks (2013 orders).

SEC award amounts in orders are what the claimant 'would' or 'will' receive based on sanctions collected at the date of the order ('more than', 'approximately'), not amounts actually paid; later collections can raise them.

Possible date issue in wave-1 rows: the FY2020 annual-report row for Exchange Act Rel. No. 88658 ($27 million) is dated 3 April 2020, while the Final Orders list and press release 2020-89 date it 16 April 2020. Wave-1 FY2020 rows note that their pairing of release numbers to awards was inferred; this was not re-checked row by row.

One document dated 8 Feb 2023 is labelled 'Award Order' (award-order-2823.pdf) in the 2024 capture of the list and 'Denial Order' (denial-order-2823.pdf) in the 2025 capture; recorded as a denial, with a note.

CFTC amounts still missing for 18 granted orders: 20-WB-01, 20-WB-03, 20-WB-06, 20-WB-09, 20-WB-10, 21-WB-01, 21-WB-03, 21-WB-04, 21-WB-05, 21-WB-06, 23-WB-01, 23-WB-04, 26-WB-02, 26-WB-20, 26-WB-21, 26-WB-25, 26-WB-26, 26-WB-27 (and 24-WB-02 has only a percentage). The orders redact the amounts, press releases 8233-20 and 8239-20 (for 20-WB-09 and 20-WB-10) name no amount, the others have no press release, and the CFTC states that it 'does not disclose the specific enforcement action or the exact award amount'. 24-WB-09 to 24-WB-12 have only a combined total (about $4.5 million for seven whistleblowers).
CFTC denial orders (about 107 orders on the whistleblower.gov list with result 'Denied') were not recorded as cases in this pass; the brief covered CFTC amounts only.
SEC press-release bodies were not downloaded; headlines from the SEC's press-release list were used only where no order or existing row gave an amount.
